samples.summary: `sheets cells get` still discards the backend error envelope, so the TYPE_MISMATCH code the design doc promises never reaches the agent
samples.evidence: The diff establishes the rule "an envelope (`error.code` string) is forwarded verbatim; anything else becomes HTTP_ERROR carrying the upstream message" for the six docs/notes/slides content+export paths. The sibling path that the design matrix pairs with them was not updated: `packages/cli/src/commands/cells.ts:25` does `if (!res.ok) throw new Error(`HTTP ${res.status}`)`, which `outputError` flattens to `{"error":{"code":"ERROR","message":"HTTP 409"}}` — dropping both the backend's `code` and its `message`. docs/design/cli.md:1029 explicitly promises `sheets.cells.get` on a doc → code `TYPE_MISMATCH`, and the same discard also loses the client's own `SESSION_EXPIRED` envelope produced at packages/cli/src/client/http-client.ts:160. So after this change `docs content` on a sheet yields TYPE_MISMATCH verbatim while the mirror-image `sheets cells get` on a doc yields `ERROR`, which is exactly the branch-on-which-command-you-ran hazard the new helper's doc comment says must not exist.

samples.summary: ~30 other CLI command sites still report a failed upstream response as code `ERROR` with a bare `HTTP <status>`, so the new HTTP_ERROR/message contract holds on only 6 of ~36 paths
samples.evidence: Unconverted sites all use `if (!res.ok) throw new Error(`HTTP ${res.status}`)`: packages/cli/src/commands/docs.ts:80,107,121,139,157; notes.ts:40,67,81,99,117; slides.ts:45,72,86,104,122; files.ts:86,106,124,142; api-keys.ts:18,32,46; tabs.ts:16,49,75; cells.ts:25,65,91,143; sheets-import.ts:87. Each yields `code: "ERROR"` and drops the upstream `message` (e.g. Nest's "Document has no file"), while the six paths in this diff now yield `code: "HTTP_ERROR"` plus the upstream text for the identical condition. Consumers that fingerprint on `error.code` (scripts/agent/hunt-fingerprint.mjs:76 keys observations off it) now see two different codes for the same failure depending on which subcommand was run.

samples.summary: `sheets export` keeps the envelope's `message` but throws away its `code`, so a real backend envelope surfaces as `ERROR`
samples.evidence: packages/cli/src/commands/sheets-export.ts:41-42 reads only `(res.data as {error?:{message?:string}})?.error?.message` and throws a plain `Error`, so `outputError` reports `code: "ERROR"` even when the backend sent `{error:{code:"TYPE_MISMATCH",…}}`. This is the third distinct treatment of the same upstream condition alongside the new `forwardUpstreamError`/`upstreamErrorJson` pair; converting it would have been a one-line change in this diff.

samples.summary: The README "Errors" contract the new helper cites as its source of truth still says every untyped failure reports `"ERROR"`
samples.evidence: packages/cli/README.md:116-120: “Typed errors (e.g., `INVALID_DOCX`, `TYPE_MISMATCH`, `CONFIRMATION_REQ`) carry a command-specific `code` agents can branch on; everything else reports `"ERROR"`.” After this change `docs/notes/slides content|export` report `HTTP_ERROR` for a non-envelope upstream body, and the formatter's own comment (packages/cli/src/output/formatter.ts:68-69) points agents at this very section as the definition of the contract. `HTTP_ERROR` is documented only in two import skill files (packages/cli/skills/docs-import-docx.md:84, slides-import-pptx.md:72), not for the read/export paths.

samples.summary: The design doc's Error Matrix has no `HTTP_ERROR` row and still promises UNAUTHORIZED/SYSTEM at exit 2 for backend 401/403/5xx, which the new path contradicts
samples.evidence: docs/design/cli.md:1038-1039 documents “Backend 401/403 → exit 2, UNAUTHORIZED” and “Backend 5xx or network → exit 2, SYSTEM”. A 401 or 500 whose body is Nest's default (no `error.code`) now goes through `forwardUpstreamError` → `UpstreamHttpError` → `outputError`, emitting `code: "HTTP_ERROR"` with `process.exitCode = 1` (packages/cli/src/output/formatter.ts:62,171). Nothing in the CLI maps status to exit 2 — I grepped `packages/cli/src` for `401`, `403`, `exitCode = 2`, `UNAUTHORIZED` and found only the client's retry/refresh logic (http-client.ts:140,181) and `SESSION_EXPIRED` (http-client.ts:160). The divergence is partly pre-existing, but this change is the one that names the code for backend failures and did not record it in the matrix.

samples.summary: The task doc driving the visual-harness change now states the opposite of what was implemented: it claims the font `check()` wait hard-fails on timeout
samples.evidence: docs/tasks/active/20260811-visual-inter-font-race-todo.md:52-56 reads “The `check()` wait already hard-fails (10s timeout) if a family never becomes available … an unreachable `fonts.googleapis.com` now reports a clear timeout instead of an opaque pixel diff.” The implementation wraps both polls in `settle()` (packages/frontend/scripts/verify-visual-browser.mjs:395,421,436-444), which downgrades a timeout to `console.warn` and shoots anyway — i.e. an unreachable font host now produces exactly the opaque pixel diff the note says it no longer will. The risk posture recorded for this change is stale.

samples.summary: Committed visual baselines were captured under the old (fallback-font) capture order and none are regenerated here
samples.evidence: packages/frontend/scripts/verify-visual-browser.mjs:479 now settles fonts after section mount and additionally waits on Inter/Fraunces/JetBrains Mono at weights 400-700, so captures can legitimately differ from the ~108 committed PNGs under packages/frontend/tests/visual/baselines/ (e.g. harness-visual.browser.slides-theme-panel.desktop.dark.png), none of which the diff touches. docs/tasks/active/20260811-visual-inter-font-race-todo.md:55 asserts the baselines already record the Inter-loaded state, which — if accurate — makes this a non-issue; I could not verify that from pixels, so surfacing it in case the assumption is wrong for the dark/mobile profiles.

finding.summary: `sheets cells get` still discards the backend error envelope, so the TYPE_MISMATCH code the design doc promises never reaches the agent
finding.evidence: The diff establishes the rule "an envelope (`error.code` string) is forwarded verbatim; anything else becomes HTTP_ERROR carrying the upstream message" for the six docs/notes/slides content+export paths. The sibling path that the design matrix pairs with them was not updated: `packages/cli/src/commands/cells.ts:25` does `if (!res.ok) throw new Error(`HTTP ${res.status}`)`, which `outputError` flattens to `{"error":{"code":"ERROR","message":"HTTP 409"}}` — dropping both the backend's `code` and its `message`. docs/design/cli.md:1029 explicitly promises `sheets.cells.get` on a doc → code `TYPE_MISMATCH`, and the same discard also loses the client's own `SESSION_EXPIRED` envelope produced at packages/cli/src/client/http-client.ts:160. So after this change `docs content` on a sheet yields TYPE_MISMATCH verbatim while the mirror-image `sheets cells get` on a doc yields `ERROR`, which is exactly the branch-on-which-command-you-ran hazard the new helper's doc comment says must not exist.

verdict.reason: The literal code exists (cells.ts:25 throws a plain `HTTP <status>` Error that outputError flattens to code ERROR), but it is not a blast-radius defect and not blocking under this lens's rubric. (a) No changed contract reaches it: the diff's new exports forwardUpstreamError/upstreamErrorJson/UpstreamHttpError (formatter.ts:137,162,186) are consumed only by docs.ts:197,249, slides.ts:154,197, notes.ts:148,195 and the import/upload/download modules; cells.ts imports only `output`/`outputError` (cells.ts:3), whose behaviour for a plain Error is unchanged, and no export it uses was renamed, removed, or given a new precondition. (b) forwardUpstreamError is an stderr formatter, not an access/permission/validation guard — there is no protected operation that cells.ts reaches around, so this is not a guard bypass. (c) The reviewer's headline scenario is counterfactual: packages/backend/src/api/v1/cells.controller.ts contains no document-type check at all (getCells :45-76 and getCell :78-103 only throw NotFoundException('Tab not found') at :58/:91); TYPE_MISMATCH is produced only by docs-content.controller.ts:42-44,88, so `sheets cells get` on a doc never yields a TYPE_MISMATCH envelope for cells.ts to discard — docs/design/cli.md:1029 is an unimplemented design-matrix row. (d) Residual real impact (a SESSION_EXPIRED 401 envelope from http-client.ts:156-164 being reported as code ERROR with message "HTTP 401") is a pre-existing, repo-wide pattern shared with docs.ts:80,107,121,139,157 and sheets-export.ts:42; the command still emits the documented {error:{code,message}} shape and exit 1, i.e. rubric-level "minor — a consumer that still works but is now inconsistent", not a broken caller or reachable bypass.

finding.summary: Real backend error messages are now discarded on every non-envelope failure (401/403/404/400 validation), because the backend has no global exception filter and returns Nest's default `{message, error:'Not Found', statusCode}` bodies
finding.evidence: The backend's v1 API throws plain Nest exceptions and no global exception filter exists (grep for `ExceptionFilter|useGlobalFilters` in packages/backend/src returned nothing). So the *common* failure bodies the CLI receives are framework-shaped, not the envelope: packages/backend/src/api/v1/files.controller.ts:141 `throw new NotFoundException('Document has no file')`, files.controller.ts:81 / documents.controller.ts:109 `throw new ForbiddenException('This API key does not have write access')`, workspace-scope.guard.ts:28 ForbiddenException, cells.controller.ts:58 `NotFoundException('Tab not found')`. Before this change `wafflebase files download <id>` / `files upload` / `docs import` printed that body, so the human/agent-readable cause ("Document has no file", "This API key does not have write access") reached stderr. After it, `upstreamErrorJson` (formatter.ts:127-132) and `forwardUpstreamError` (formatter.ts:109) drop the body entirely and emit only `{error:{code:'HTTP_ERROR'|'ERROR', message:'HTTP 404'}}`. Only the code shape is fixed; the diagnostic text is lost for every real backend error except the two hand-built envelopes (TYPE_MISMATCH, SESSION_EXPIRED). docs/design/cli.md:1039 documents the opposite intent for backend failures — "(original message preserved)". The fix belongs on the new helpers: carry the framework body's `message` (and `statusCode`) into the envelope's `message` instead of throwing it away.

verdict.reason: The described code is not present. The finding says `upstreamErrorJson`/`forwardUpstreamError` drop the upstream body and emit only `{error:{code:'HTTP_ERROR',message:'HTTP 404'}}`, losing text like "Document has no file". In the repository, `upstreamDetail` (formatter.ts:104-121) extracts `body.message` — string, plain-string body, or class-validator string array joined with "; " — truncated at 500 chars and skipping HTML pages; `upstreamMessage` (formatter.ts:124-127) returns `HTTP <status>: <detail>` whenever a detail exists. `forwardUpstreamError` throws `UpstreamHttpError(upstreamMessage(res), res.status)` (formatter.ts:171) and `upstreamErrorJson` emits `{error:{code:'HTTP_ERROR', message: upstreamMessage(res)}}` (formatter.ts:191-195). The reviewer's cited lines do not contain the claimed behaviour: :109 is the array-join branch of `upstreamDetail`, and :127-132 is the end of `upstreamMessage` plus the `UpstreamHttpError` doc comment. The backend premise checks out (no ExceptionFilter/useGlobalFilters in packages/backend/src), but it is moot because the CLI already preserves the framework body's message — the exact fix the finding proposes. Tests assert this directly: upstream-error.test.ts:80-87 expects 'HTTP 404: Document has no file', :89-96 the validation-array join, :241-245 and :247-255 the same for `upstreamErrorJson` ('HTTP 403: Forbidden resource'). Only one formatter.ts exists in the tree, so no stale duplicate accounts for the discrepancy.

finding.summary: Adding index.html's own families (Inter/Fraunces/JetBrains Mono) to the font gate makes every visual capture, in every section, hard-depend on fonts.googleapis.com resolving within 10s
finding.evidence: packages/frontend/index.html:12 requests Inter/Fraunces/JetBrains Mono on every page load, so those FontFaces are registered for *all* harness pages, not just slides sections. Previously the polled set was only the four families useGoogleFontsLink() injects (so `document.fonts.check` matched nothing and returned true trivially on the ~200 non-slides captures). Now, if the css2 stylesheet loads but the font binaries fail or are slow (restricted-network CI, cold cache), the faces stay unloaded/errored and the new `waitForFunction(..., {timeout: 10000})` at verify-visual-browser.mjs:384 fails for every one of the 220 baselines under packages/frontend/tests/visual/baselines/, not just the two sections that drifted. The swallowed `.catch(() => {})` on `fonts.load` (line 374) removes the previous fast failure, so the symptom becomes a timeout per page. Worth confirming the visual lane has egress to fonts.googleapis.com; otherwise the enumerated set should be limited to families the section under capture actually registers, or the poll should tolerate errored faces.

verdict.reason: The finding's central mechanism is not present in the code. It claims a new `waitForFunction(..., {timeout: 10000})` at verify-visual-browser.mjs:384 hard-fails every capture when fonts.googleapis.com is slow/unreachable. Line 384 is actually `};` (end of the `loadPass` closure). The real font-check poll lives at :396-405 and is NOT awaited directly — it is passed to `settle(...)` at :395, as is the second "no face still loading" poll at :421-428. `settle()` (:436-444) catches any error matching /Timeout .* exceeded|timeout/i, logs `console.warn("[visual] fonts did not settle — …")` naming the pending families, and returns normally; only non-timeout errors re-throw. Playwright's waitForFunction timeout message ("page.waitForFunction: Timeout 10000ms exceeded.") matches that regex. The sole caller, captureProfile at :479, therefore proceeds to screenshot at :481-489 regardless. The premises the reviewer got right — index.html:12 requesting Inter/Fraunces/JetBrains Mono on every page load, and those families being added to VISUAL_FONT_FAMILIES at :350-360 — do not produce the claimed consequence, because the capture never hard-depends on the host answering. Worst case is added wall-clock plus a warning (and a font-driven baseline diff), which is not a broken caller, bypassed guard, or violated invariant under the blast-radius rubric.
